verdict: Weyerhaeuser's sales rose 8% to $1.9 billion on stronger wood-products demand, but net earnings fell to $61 million because last year's quarter included $63 million of one-off gains — a lumber mill sale and insurance recoveries — that did not repeat.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: net sales, +8.4% vs a year ago

segments.name: Timberlands
segments.note: Logs and timber from Weyerhaeuser's own forests in the West, South and North, sold to outside customers (another $153M was sold internally to Wood Products and is eliminated in consolidation).

segments.name: Strategic Land Solutions
segments.note: Selling surplus land, mineral and energy rights, and climate projects such as forest carbon credits — the segment renamed from Real Estate, Energy & Natural Resources in 2026.

segments.name: Wood Products
segments.note: Lumber, oriented strand board, engineered wood products and building-materials distribution — by far the biggest business.

opex.name: Selling expenses
opex.note: The cost of selling lumber, panels and logs.

opex.name: General and administrative expenses
opex.note: The back office: finance, legal, IT and head-office staff.

opex.name: Other operating costs, net
opex.note: Litigation expense of $8M, research of $2M and $6M of other items. A year ago this line was $49M of income, including a mill-sale gain and insurance recoveries.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $63M and $15M of non-operating pension costs, partly offset by $3M of other income — and by the quarter's $36M income-tax benefit, which this chart nets into this line (see the note below). Net: $39M of expense below operating profit.
oneTimers: No special items in Q3 2026: GAAP net earnings of $61M equal net earnings before special items. A year ago, other operating income included a $29M gain on a lumber mill sale and $34M of insurance recoveries, which flatter the year-ago comparison.
After quarter-end, Weyerhaeuser agreed to sell about 81,000 acres of non-core Arkansas timberlands for $146M, with closing expected in the fourth quarter of 2026.

takeaways.title: Wood Products carried sales
takeaways.text: Wood Products sales rose 13% to $1,385M and its contribution to earnings swung to +$32M from −$19M a year ago, as lumber and panel markets improved.

takeaways.title: Cash earnings rose
takeaways.text: Adjusted EBITDA — a non-GAAP cash-earnings yardstick — rose 14% to $248M even as GAAP earnings fell, because last year's GAAP result held one-off gains that did not repeat.

takeaways.title: Selling non-core land
takeaways.text: Weyerhaeuser is selling about 81,000 acres in Arkansas for $146M (closing expected in Q4), while monetizing roughly 340,000 forest carbon credits so far this year and starting construction of its first biocarbon facility.

footerNote: Weyerhaeuser is a real estate investment trust (REIT). Net earnings of $61M are the consolidated figure attributable to common shareholders. Income taxes were a $36M benefit — the REIT structure leaves most timber income untaxed at the company level — so the printed statement steps from $25M of pre-tax income up to $61M of net earnings. This chart nets that $36M benefit into Other income (the tax line therefore reads $0) instead of drawing a negative tax band. Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted FAD are non-GAAP measures reconciled in the release. Segment sales are sales to unaffiliated customers from the 10-Q segment note.
